facility.name: Creative Learning Center
facility.programs_provided: School Age Care,Before School Care,Meals Provided ,After School Care,Snacks Provided,Part Time Care,Transportation to/from School ,Field Trips

provenance.note: Census Geocoder Non_Exact match: 11401 US HWY 290, MANOR, TX, 78653

inspection_summary.note: Texas HHSC inspections, report investigations and assessments since October 2017, updated daily.

occurrences.finding: Prohibited Punishments - Using Harsh, Abusive or Profane Language: It was determined that caregivers were using profane language in the presence of children in care.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Prohibited Punishments - Humiliating, Rejecting, Yelling (26 TAC §746.2805(6))

occurrences.finding: Children Handwashing After Toileting or Diapering: One caregiver was observed to have not washed a child's hands after diapering. This was fixed at inspection when the caregiver washed the child's hands after being asked by the CCR inspector.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Children Handwashing After Toileting or Diapering (26 TAC §746.3417(3))

occurrences.finding: Medication No Longer Used: At the time of the inspection, one medication stored at the operation was expired. It was sent home during the inspection.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Medication No Longer Used (26 TAC §746.3809)

occurrences.finding: Licensing Incident/Illness Report Form - Situations Placing Children at Risk: The operation did not notify parents of an incident that may have placed a child at risk.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Licensing Incident/Illness Report Form - Situations Placing Children at Risk (26 TAC §746.701(5))

occurrences.finding: Prohibited Punishments - Humiliating, Rejecting, Yelling: It was determined that caregivers were observed yelling at children in care.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Prohibited Punishments - Humiliating, Rejecting, Yelling (26 TAC §746.2805(5))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control: It was determined a caregiver used poor judgement when redirecting children.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control (26 TAC §746.1201(1))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control: It was determined that a caregiver used poor judgement while caring for children.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control (26 TAC §746.1201(1))

occurrences.finding: Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance - Brief Supervised Separation: It was determined that a caregiver was using inappropriately long timeouts for children in care.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance - Brief Supervised Separation (26 TAC §746.2803(4)(D))

occurrences.finding: Parental Notification of Less Serious Injuries: During the investigation, it was found that the management staff did not discuss an injury with the parent by phone or during pick-up.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Parental Notification of Less Serious Injuries (26 TAC §746.307(c))

occurrences.finding: Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance - Brief Supervised Separation: During the investigation, it was found that a caregiver was placing 2-year-olds in timeout for 5 minutes for misbehaving.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance - Brief Supervised Separation (26 TAC §746.2803(4)(D))

occurrences.finding: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity: A child was able to exit the building through an emergency exit door in the classroom without the caregiver noticing.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: Employee Handwashing After Diapering a Child: Based on the DFPS investigation, a caregiver was observed wearing the same pair of gloves while changing multiple children's diapers and did not wash their hands between changes.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Employee Handwashing After Diapering a Child (26 TAC §746.3415(4))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control: There are concerns that a caregiver was observed aggressively sitting children down in their chairs and lifting children by the arm after diaper changes.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control (26 TAC §746.1201(1))

occurrences.finding: Children Handwashing After Toileting or Diapering: Based on the DFPS investigation, a caregiver was observed on video surveillance not washing children's hands after changing their diapers.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Children Handwashing After Toileting or Diapering (26 TAC §746.3417(3))

occurrences.finding: Prohibited Punishments - Corporal Punishment: Based on the DFPS investigation, 2 caregivers were observed on video footage hitting children in their care.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Prohibited Punishments - Corporal Punishment (26 TAC §746.2805(1))

occurrences.finding: Documented Annual Training- Required Content: 3 caregivers did not have the required training topics at the time of the inspection.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Documented Annual Training- Required Content (26 TAC §746.1309(e))

occurrences.finding: Children's Products- Annual Certification: The operation has not certified annually in writing using the Children's Product Certification form provided by HHSC that they have reviewed each of the recall notices issued by the CPSC. This was corrected when the Children's Product Certification Form was emailed to the director to complete.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Children's Products- Annual Certification (26 TAC §746.4135(b))

occurrences.finding: AP Cribs - Only Snug Fitting Sheet and Crib Mattress Cover Allowed if Infant Younger than 12 Months of Age: One infant was sleeping in a crib with a noise machine. This was corrected when the caregiver removed the noise machine from the crib.
occurrences.violation_type_title: AP Cribs - Only Snug Fitting Sheet and Crib Mattress Cover Allowed if Infant Younger than 12 Months of Age (26 TAC §746.2415(b))

occurrences.finding: AP Infants Sleep on Backs or Must Have Completed and Signed Sleep Exception Form for the Infant: An infant was placed in a crib on their stomach with the intention of the infant falling asleep. This was corrected when the infant was turned over on their back.
occurrences.violation_type_title: AP Infants Sleep on Backs or Must Have Completed and Signed Sleep Exception Form for the Infant (26 TAC §746.2427)

occurrences.finding: AP Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Ensure No Child Abused, Neglected, or Exploited: Based on the DFPS investigation, it was determined that a child was abused in care which resulted in an injury.
occurrences.violation_type_title: AP Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Ensure No Child Abused, Neglected, or Exploited (26 TAC §746.1201(4))

occurrences.finding: Prohibited Punishments - Humiliating, Rejecting, Yelling: Based on the DFPS investigation, there is enough evidence to determine a caregiver was yelling at the children in care.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Prohibited Punishments - Humiliating, Rejecting, Yelling (26 TAC §746.2805(5))

occurrences.finding: Prohibited Punishments - Corporal Punishment: Based on the DFPS investigation, it was determined that a caregiver pinched a child which caused an injury
occurrences.violation_type_title: Prohibited Punishments - Corporal Punishment (26 TAC §746.2805(1))

occurrences.finding: Training Requirements for Employees and Caregivers - Pre-service Training: 1 of 10 personnel files reviewed was missing 5 of the required Pre-service hours required within the first 90 days.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Training Requirements for Employees and Caregivers - Pre-service Training (26 TAC §746.1301(2)(A))

occurrences.finding: Written Feeding Instructions - Review and Update Every 30 Days: 7 of 8 infant feeding instructions had not been updated within the past 30 days.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Written Feeding Instructions - Review and Update Every 30 Days (26 TAC §746.2421(b))

occurrences.finding: AP Background check results - Must receive notification prior to allowing subject to be present at your operation: Caregiver observed supervising children in care with a pending background check on file.
occurrences.violation_type_title: AP Background check results - Must receive notification prior to allowing subject to be present at your operation (26 TAC §745.641)

occurrences.finding: AP Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Ensure No Child Abused, Neglected, or Exploited: During a DFPS investigation, there was sufficient evidence to support that a caregiver neglectfully supervised a child in care.
occurrences.violation_type_title: AP Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Ensure No Child Abused, Neglected, or Exploited (26 TAC §746.1201(4))

occurrences.finding: Nutrition and Food Service - Must not serve identified foods to allergic child: During a DFPS investigation, there was sufficient evidence to support that a caregiver served a child food identified on the child's allergy emergency plan which caused the child to go into anaphylactic shock.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Nutrition and Food Service - Must not serve identified foods to allergic child (26 TAC §746.3301(i))

occurrences.finding: Report Situation Placing Children at Risk: The operation fail to contact CCR when a teacher unknowingly left one of her students in the classroom.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Report Situation Placing Children at Risk (26 TAC §746.305(a)(6))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Caregivers- Supervision of Children: It was determined that a caregiver was not appropriately supervising the children in her group when one of the students were left in the classroom.     The owner was walking the halls when she saw the child in the classroom. The owner took over supervision until the child returned to their group.     It is unknown how long the child was left alone.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Supervision of Children (26 TAC §746.1203(4))
